pki.transport.https.reason: The shared fail-closed node:https transport is the toolkit's sole socket choke point, still actively hardened as each new protocol client composes it and surfaces a new fail-closed requirement -- this release added another consumer in the CMC exchange carried over EST. Graduate once the network-client transport contract is settled across every consumer.

pki.est.cacerts.reason: The EST namespace is held to one decision rather than split: its verbs ride the still-experimental shared pki.transport, and graduating half a namespace while the other half moves would leave operators unable to reason about the surface as a whole. Graduate the namespace alongside pki.transport.https once the network-client surface is settled.

pki.cmc.verify.reason: Ships in this release, and no independent implementation exists to interoperate against: OpenSSL has no CMC support at all and NSS ships no RFC 5272 PKIData/PKIResponse generator, so the interop harness can cross-check only the CMS carrier, not the CMC message inside it. Graduate once a CMC oracle exists and the surface has run for a release.

pki.schema.cmc.parse.reason: Ships in this release with no independent CMC implementation to interoperate against. The RFC 6402 OtherStatusInfo ambiguity it resolves by inspection is exactly the kind of decision a second implementation would test, and none is available yet. Graduate once a CMC oracle exists.

pki.schema.c509.parse.reason: The governing document is an IETF draft (draft-ietf-cose-cbor-encoded-cert), not a published RFC, so the wire format can still change under this decoder. No C509 toolchain exists to interoperate against either. Graduate once the draft is published as an RFC.

pki.schema.c509.encode.reason: The governing document is an IETF draft (draft-ietf-cose-cbor-encoded-cert), not a published RFC, so the bytes this emits can still change with the draft. Graduate once the draft is published as an RFC.

pki.lint.certificate.reason: The call shape is settled but the rule set is not: the full CABF corpus, the S/MIME baseline requirements, and the CRL/OCSP profiles are still to land, and each one changes what this reports for an unchanged certificate. An operator gating on its output would see that as a behaviour change. Graduate once the rule set is complete.

pki.lint.rules.reason: Enumerates a rule set that is still growing toward the full CABF corpus, the S/MIME baseline requirements, and the CRL/OCSP profiles. Graduate alongside pki.lint.certificate once the rule set is complete.

This verb additionally composes the still-experimental shared pki.transport. Graduate once the CT namespace's standard footing is resolved and the transport contract settles.

pki.path.build.reason: Path building itself is settled, but its opt-in AIA caIssuers fetching composes the still-experimental shared pki.transport, and that is the part of its contract still absorbing hardening. The default offline build is unchanged and every path it returns is decided by the now-stable pki.path.validate. Graduate alongside pki.transport.https.

pki.webauthn.verifyAssertion.reason: The ceremony this verifies is settled in WebAuthn Level 3, but its own verdict shape is not: the fields a relying party reads to decide what was checked have changed in three of the last four releases, most recently when the two accepted forms of a stored credential key were brought under one set of rules. An operator gating on the verdict would have seen each of those as a behaviour change. Graduate once a release passes without the verdict shape moving.

pki.webauthn.parseAuthenticatorData.reason: Held to the same decision as pki.webauthn.verifyAssertion, which consumes it: the parsed shape gained surfaced fields as the verifier's verdict grew, so it moved for the same reasons. Graduate alongside pki.webauthn.verifyAssertion.

pki.webauthn.parseClientData.reason: Held to the same decision as pki.webauthn.verifyAssertion, which consumes it. Graduate alongside pki.webauthn.verifyAssertion.
